title: Adult dehydration workflow test
opening: A 32-year-old adult comes to the emergency department after two days of vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, and reduced oral intake.
appearance: The patient appears tired, thirsty, and mildly uncomfortable but is alert and able to answer questions.

history.History of Present Illness: The patient reports two days of nonbloody vomiting and watery diarrhea after a shared meal. Oral intake has been poor. There is lightheadedness when standing but no syncope.
history.Past Medical History: No chronic medical conditions or prior hospitalizations.
history.Personal/Social History: No tobacco or recreational drug use. Drinks alcohol occasionally.
history.Review of Systems: No chest pain, dyspnea, focal abdominal pain, blood in stool, dysuria, rash, or recent antibiotic use.

exam.General Appearance: Alert and tired appearing. Mucous membranes are dry.
exam.HEENT/Neck: Dry oral mucosa. Neck is supple.
exam.Heart/Cardiovascular: Tachycardic with a regular rhythm. Peripheral pulses are present.
exam.Chest/Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal work of breathing.
exam.Abdomen: Soft with mild diffuse discomfort and no guarding, rebound, or focal tenderness.
exam.Neuro/Psych: Alert and oriented with no focal neurologic deficit.
exam.Skin: Warm with mildly reduced skin turgor. No rash.

orders.name: Counseling, oral hydration and return precautions

results.value: Sodium 136 mEq/L; potassium 3.4 mEq/L; bicarbonate 20 mEq/L; BUN 26 mg/dL; creatinine 1.1 mg/dL; glucose 94 mg/dL.
Concentrated urine with specific gravity 1.030; no leukocyte esterase, nitrites, blood, or protein.

scoreRules.label: Focused abdominal examination
scoreRules.rationale: A focused examination helps assess for focal tenderness or peritoneal findings.

scoreRules.label: Establish IV access
scoreRules.rationale: IV access supports prompt fluid administration.

scoreRules.label: Administer isotonic fluid
scoreRules.rationale: Isotonic fluid addresses clinically significant volume depletion.

scoreRules.label: Treat ongoing nausea
scoreRules.rationale: Controlling nausea may help the patient resume oral hydration.

scoreRules.label: Evaluate electrolytes and renal function
scoreRules.rationale: Laboratory assessment helps characterize dehydration and electrolyte disturbance.

scoreRules.label: Obtain blood count
scoreRules.rationale: A blood count contributes to the initial evaluation.

scoreRules.label: Provide hydration counseling and return precautions
scoreRules.rationale: Discharge instructions support continued recovery and escalation when needed.

scoreRules.label: Choose home disposition after stabilization
scoreRules.rationale: A stable patient who can tolerate oral intake may complete recovery at home.

scoreRules.label: Unnecessary empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic
scoreRules.rationale: The presentation does not establish an indication for empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy.

feedback: The intended workflow is focused assessment, correction of volume depletion, symptom control, review of delayed laboratory results, hydration counseling, and an appropriate disposition after stabilization. This fictional case is for software-flow testing and requires clinician review before educational publication.
